items.note: N0 states the lemma (forward invocation y<-y+x for arbitrary scratch, three stages giving (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) with every auxiliary restored, a plain swap over F_2), and N0.1-N0.4 follow the proof at 741-765 step by step: the net change (JV+RG)x, the bit coefficients |S cap T| mod 2, the complex coefficients (|S cap T|-1)/2, and the chain (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x). The setup parameters (h=100, N, the neighbour rules as definitions) and the neighbour and wire counts at 767-782 are not given, but they are not part of the lemma itself.

F0 states the common-frame identity D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and F0.1-F0.4 reproduce the invariant proof: the logical input is D_in^{-1} f with no preprocessing, a common frame commutes with a pointwise linear gate, and each route applies eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}, scratch roles included.

Everything the item states is present: the nondegenerate labels in F^{tensor 3} of dimension m=h^3, the forms (I-J/9 over Q, the dot product over F_2), nested labels on every edge, the only decreasing edges being centre 3->4 with loss h, L=Ich, the sum Wm-2N+2L, and the ratios 100/539 and 101/539. The derivation gives the interstage consistency, the side-wire nesting and the telescoping count, but leaves out the time-indexed gate-label table (975-988) and the residual table (1021-1043) that actually establish which edges decrease. L0 only says to 'read every edge's residual from a table', and the orthonormal-basis argument (1073-1102) is restated without proof.

B0 states the proposition: pointwise XOR gates, the role permutation rho, M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m, and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m. B0.1-B0.4 follow the proof: rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, the N exceptional source edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one, the deficit N-2L_b, and the endpoint difference P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m. K0.2 supplies the shear H<-H+D on every role.

P0 and its sub-steps give the phase frames, one kernel aI+bX_v (or its inverse) per orthonormal residual vector, s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c<W_c m, and the endpoint corrections: C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a), the Z_{a,k} and i^{27k} wrappers, then negating the X outputs. P0's headline claims C^{tensor m} on every role without these corrections (listed as a minor error), but P0.6-P0.8 state them exactly as at 1290-1314.

The plan gives L/N<1/2, the deficits N-2L_b>0 and 2N-2L_c>0, s<Wm in both networks, and B0.5's chain: both relative deficits exceed 20*2^{-50} and m<2^{20}, so m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20*2^{-50})>m(1-eta), giving s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}. This is the paper's route at 1331-1344. The exact fractions eta_b=339/22587335000000 and eta_c=73/19906842167500 are not displayed, only the bound they satisfy.

S1.1 matches the four elementary operations of Lemma lem:elementary-streams. S1.2 states the O(V) controlled shift and fixed-unit scaling with a one-clause reason (one split and merge of blocks, as at 575-581). It drops the conditions that the offset be preparable in b^{O(1)} time and that the denominators (and the unit numerators) be prime to q. There is no method or sub-steps, so this counts as stated.

T0 gives A=E_1 Pi E_2 by the paper's pivot elimination (topmost nonzero row, rightmost entry, active indices). MS0.1-MS0.4 give the choice of prime, linear-cost triangular maps in descending order, the conjugation order, and the three-step realization of each one in Pi using exactly one interchange, so exactly a interchanges plus O(V).

Every element of the proof is present: the cyclic row split into W role streams of volume V/W, frames Phi_{M_v} giving Phi_{I_m}, i.e. H<-H+D on every row including scratch rows, the three shears D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D, s calls, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) with both cases of the geometric sum, and the O(V) fixed-tape parking schedule. K0's headline names only s<Wm from the contract. The endpoint identity is carried by B0 and used in K0.2.

S1.4.1-S1.4.6 reproduce the proof: k and rho=ceil(k log W/(2 log q)), the high digits forming a row field R=q^{2 rho}>=W^k padded to R'<2R, base-m pieces of width m^j, the geometric sum O(V e^tau), binary padding to [q^e], and the one-bit peel for unequal widths.

Y0.1-Y0.5 give the conjugation by P_M, one forward child per residual vector via (C^{-1})^{tensor f}=(-i)^f Z C Z, at most m(m-1)+3m row additions, exactly s_c children on f=e/m axes, and H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D. The slot and column layout (1867-1876) is left implicit in 'one slot'.

The plan follows the proof: the eight conditional additions composing to a parity flip with w restored, each line being one cyclic chunk shift after at most two swaps, the guard interval 10<=g<=2^{K-1}-11, delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}}, T_0 S_0^{-1} permuting B, radix-sort repair, the stated time and its o(1) extra terms, and the application to row additions at O(V((eK)^tau+1)).

Z0.1-Z0.10 reproduce the leaf cost O(Ve), the node overhead, q_0 row chunks, children of volume V/W, F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), the internal and leaf sums with a<=m^sigma, the base-m pieces and the final O(d^{lambda'}) with the stated condition on lambda'.

B0x states the layer, O(V d^{lambda'}) and one final truncation, and B0x.1 the error below sqrt2 2^{-p}. G0-G0.5 derive Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1})=o(p) from A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E, the B^{k+1} bound and the denominator/modulus induction, with epsilon C_1<1. This is the paper's assembly at 2686-2758. B0x's method misstates the child count per edge (minor error).

C1 and its sub-steps cover character cancellation by the index shift, the DIF recursion, the bit-reversed storage B_t, the reverse procedure giving F^+ B^{-1}, and the grouped round with J_E. C2 and its sub-steps cover the layout L (prefix moves, at most Dq-1 chunk exchanges), the per-round layer cost, the prefix rounds, the monomial by split and merge, J_E Q_p=Q_p J_E, the error sqrt2 ell 2^{-p}, and the stored order L(Bj).

Steps C3.1-C3.7 follow the proof: evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, the separation bound |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<B_0/2, two's-complement encoding with carries in {-1,0}, centred extraction with carries in {0,1}, the numerators ac-be and ae+bc reduced negacyclically, and truncation by a shift, with cost O(rp log(rp)).

C states the error sqrt2 M(3ell+1)2^{-p} and the cost. C.1-C.7 give the normalization identity, P(LBu,LBv)=LB P(u,v), the error chain 2delta, 2delta+eta, 3delta+eta, M(3delta+eta), and the M=T/r products. This matches 3414-3495.

The identity P_s F_s=2^{2alpha^2} B_0 P_t F_t A, the hypotheses, the errors (p^2, dp^2), the times, the tensor form with gamma=2d alpha^2, and the O(d^2) axis exposure at O(Tp(1+ell^tau)) each are all stated. The derivation (N=CTD, Neumann series, the normalizations S'/2, N^{-1}/2, 2^{-(2alpha^2-2)}D, the ordered selection C, retaining the sorts) follows 3576-3697. The plan never defines the retained permutations (P_s u)_j=u_{tj} and (P_t v)_k=v_{-sk}, although they are the point of the lemma.

H1 and H2 state both identities and the conjugation trick. The sub-steps give the periodicity, the coefficient comparison against Q reading frequency (-s_i j_i), F^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F^+, RF^+R=F^+, the commutation of the permutation with pointwise products, and the normalized convolution rule giving (u*v)/S^2.

PB/PB.1/PB.2 list the fixed rationals and sizes (Tp=Theta(n), d, K, ell, r). Q1 and its sub-steps derive the prime intervals with eta=1/(4d) (HvdH Lemma 5.1), disjointness, T/2<S<T by Bernoulli, alpha^4 theta_i>p, and the n^{o(1)} search. gamma<=b/4 is used in ER.9. The no-wraparound degree bound appears only in M0's method.

Q2 and its sub-steps give the isomorphism x->prod x_i^{mu_i}, the triangular digits b_i=a_i+mu_i sum_{j<i} a_j P_j mod s_i, the padding scan, the update order i=d..1, the cyclic shifts of valid intervals preserving the padding, and the O(Tp d^2(1+ell^tau)) cost.

The plan states Theta: x_d->zeta y as a well-defined, diagonal, norm-preserving isomorphism, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j, M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T, and the computed twist sequence. The twist error bound below 4 is given in ER.2.

X0-X0.3 give the computed chirp transform, the source transform A, C, B_0, 2^gamma with exact counterpart RF_s, and the conjugated opposite procedure. M1-M6 give the six steps as written, and M7 explains the two occurrences of S as at 4536-4541.

The error chain is reproduced with the paper's constants: E_ring=M(3L+2)<5TL, then 6TL, 8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, (3E_s+2), E_w<28*2^gamma T^2 L, and the final bound 448b 2^{-b+gamma}<=448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2. The rounding to c_j<2^{3b}, the carry invariant and the 2n-bit output follow.

PB.3-PB.14 reproduce the table rows and their powers, the margins g_1..g_7 with min g_2=2^{-181}=2kappa, the setup and exceptional-stream o(V) bounds, absorption of fixed powers of log p into p^kappa, and the schoolbook cutoff, giving O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}).
S0 says the bound disproves the n log n optimality conjecture in this model but never states the eventual-lower-bound formulation or the liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n)=0 criterion.

errors.says: The method says the complex network's edge frames are products of two-point kernels on groups of f=e/m axes 'so that each edge costs one smaller layer'.
errors.paper: An edge costs one child layer per vector of an orthonormal basis of its residual (rho_edge kernels, including on decreasing edges), and summing the residual dimensions gives s_c children per invocation, not one per edge.

errors.says: The endpoint operator is C^{tensor m} on every role.
errors.paper: Only after source and sink diagonal corrections and undoing the signed bank exchange. Before them, the route X_a->Y_a carries C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a), and the X outputs carry a minus sign. P0.6-P0.8 restore this.

errors.says: It assumes a fixed restoring circuit whose edge matrices have total rank s<Wm, and chooses tau with s/W<m^tau.
errors.paper: The contract eq:finite-shear-contract also requires the endpoint identity M_out(rho(w))-M_in(w)=I_m on every role, and q must avoid the denominators of every terminal and gate matrix. The endpoint identity is what makes every role receive the same shear H<-H+D.

errors.says: Updating y->y+a (mod q^b) by an offset from earlier control fields, or multiplying by a fixed rational unit, costs O(V).
errors.paper: This holds provided the offset can be prepared in b^{O(1)} time from the control values, with denominators prime to q (and numerators prime to q for units).

errors.says: Since L<N/2 the label total Wm-2N+2L is strictly below Wm, and this strict deficit is the source of the power saving.
errors.paper: The label total would be below Wm for any L<N. L<N/2 is needed because the rational interface adds N extra source ranks, so the operative bit deficit is N-2L_b (s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b), while the complex deficit is 2N-2L_c.

chain: The tree reaches the main bound by the paper's route. On the movement side it goes from the bit network (N0, F0, L0, R0, B0) through matrix shears and the power-width recurrence (MS0, K0, PR0) to arbitrary widths (S1.4). On the arithmetic side it goes from the complex phase network through phase frames, packed bit addition, the layer recurrence and guard widths to the simultaneous layer (P0, Y0, A0, Z0, G0). From there it continues through synthetic transforms, ring convolution, resampling, chirp and CRT maps, the six-step algorithm, exact recovery and the cost table (C, G, Q1, Q2, X0, M1-M7, ER0, PB). It thins out at the foundation: h=100, N and W are never defined, so N is used without a definition. The label construction's gate-label and residual tables and the orthonormal-basis argument are asserted rather than shown. B0x's method also misstates the number of children per edge.

steps.note: The exchange (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) with every scratch wire restored is fully described, with its three-stage mechanism, and L0 gives m=h^3 and the triple subsets. The defining parameters h=100 and N=binom(h,3)^3, and the indexing of the data pairs by a in T^3, are never stated, yet N is used throughout. I chose the conservative verdict for that reason.

A common frame per gate commutes with a pointwise linear gate, so the network implements D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}. Each edge only changes the frame by D_v D_u^{-1}, and the intermediate frames are free to make the edges cheap.
Nondegenerate labels in F^{tensor 3} of dimension m=h^3, nested along every edge, with the only decreasing edges being the central wires from time 3 to 4, each losing h.
rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U for nested labels, so an edge's cost is its dimension change. The N negative source projections are the exceptions, each first X_a edge being 2P_{U_a} of rank one.
The sum of absolute dimension changes is Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich, from the signed telescoping and the Ic decreasing edges. Adding the N source ranks gives s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2, so the deficit N-2L_b>0 (and 2N-2L_c>0) and s<Wm.
M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m on every role (P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m on X_a, 0 to I elsewhere). With frames Phi_M this makes the bit network apply H<-H+D on every role and row.
A=E_1 Pi E_2 with lower triangular factors, and the shear by a rank-a matrix costs exactly a interchanges plus O(V). Each unit of edge rank is one recursive call, so a node makes s calls.
The children have volume V/W, so F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1). s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50} from relative deficits above 20*2^{-50} and m<2^{20} (log m<20), so F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: The plan reconstructs eight of the nine steps of the central saving in the paper's order: frames, labels, rank equals dimension change, the budget with L=Ich and the extra N source ranks, L/N<1/2 giving s<Wm, the endpoint identity giving H<-H+D, edges as exactly s recursive calls, and the volume-normalized recurrence with tau=1-2^{-50}. The one weak link is C1. The bank-exchange network and its restoration are spelled out, but h=100 and N=binom(h,3)^3 are never stated even though N is used throughout, so C1 is only credited as mentioned.
